title: Expert Consensus on Key Terminology in the Field of Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine (TCIM) in Germany
summary:
Alongside conventional medicine, there are many other medical approaches: 
from phytotherapy and osteopathy to Traditional Chinese Medicine. These 
practices are grouped under various terms that are often used inconsistently. 
What exactly is "integrative medicine"? What is the difference between 
"complementary" and "alternative" medicine? Even experts frequently disagree.

In this study, we work with approximately 50-80 experts from academia, clinical 
practice, professional associations, health insurance, and the general public 
to develop shared definitions for the most important German terms in this 
field. We use the Delphi method, where experts evaluate definition proposals in 
several pseudonymised online survey rounds until broad agreement is reached (>70% consensus.
conditions: Terminology research in the field of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine (TCIM); no disease entity, no patient recruitment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least one of the following conditions must be met:
(A) Researcher or clinician with demonstrable expertise in TCIM/naturopathy: professor or chair holder in TCIM/naturopathy in Germany; or habilitated with research focus on TCIM/naturopathy; or at least 10 peer-reviewed publications in TCIM/naturopathy; or at least 1 peer-reviewed publication and 10 years of clinical experience in TCIM/naturopathy – and member of ACoNIG or the Forum of University Working Groups for Naturopathy and Integrative Medicine.
(B) Chair of a German-speaking professional association in the TCIM/naturopathy field.
(C) Representative of a statutory or private health insurance with responsibility for TCIM services or prevention.
(D) Representative of a health policy organisation or healthcare decision-making body (e.g. Federal Joint Committee G-BA, medical chamber, consumer protection, patient representation).
(E) TCIM patient or representative of the general public with heterogeneous background (age, education, region, experience with TCIM).
For all categories: willingness to participate in all survey rounds; availability for structured online participation; informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of subject-matter expertise in naturopathy and integrative medicine; exclusively administrative role without substantive involvement; relevant conflicts of interest that could compromise independent assessment; unwillingness to participate in all survey rounds; absence of informed consent.
